translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Joel son of Bethuel.
Hear this, elders, and listen, all inhabitants of the land! Has anything like this happened in your days or in the days of your ancestors?
Tell your children about it, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.
What the stripping locust left, the flying locust ate; what the flying locust left, the crawling locust ate; and what the crawling locust left, the cricket ate.
Wake up, drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you wine drinkers, over the wine that has been taken from your mouths.
For a nation has come up against my land, powerful and beyond counting. Its teeth are like a lion’s teeth, and its fangs are like the fangs of a young lion.
It has devastated my vine and stripped my fig tree. It stripped it bare and threw it away, and its branches turned white.
Lament like a virgin dressed in sackcloth over the husband of her youth.
Fine flour and drink offerings have disappeared from the house of the Lord. Kings sit in mourning, along with the priests who minister to the Lord.
The field has been ravaged, and the land sits in mourning, because the grain has been ravaged, the wine has dried up, and the olive trees have been ruined.
Be ashamed, farmers, and wail, vine growers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.
The vine has dried up, and the fig tree has withered. The pomegranate trees, palm trees, apple trees, and all the trees of the field have dried up, because joy has ceased among human beings.

Priests, put on sackcloth and mourn! Wail, servants of the altar! Come in and spend the night in sackcloth, servants of my God, because fine flour and drink offerings have been withheld from the house of your God.
Set apart a fast; call an assembly. Gather, elders and all inhabitants of the land, at the house of the Lord your God. Cry out to the Lord your God and say:
Alas, alas for the day! For the day of the Lord is near, and devastation will come from God.
Look! Food has disappeared before our eyes, and joy and rejoicing from the house of our God.
The heifers are parched at their mangers. The storehouses are ruined, the presses are demolished, and the grain has dried up.
Why do the livestock groan, and the herds of cattle cry? Because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep have perished.
To you, Lord, I cry, because fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness, and flame has burned all the trees of the open country.
Even the wild animals cry out to you, because the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.
Blow the trumpet in Zion and sound the alarm on my holy mountain! Let all inhabitants of the land tremble, because the day of the Lord has arrived and is near.

A day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness! Like dawn spread over the mountains comes a great and powerful nation. Nothing like it has ever existed, and nothing like it will come after it for generations upon generations.
Fire consumes before it, and flame burns behind it. Before it the land is like the garden of Eden, but behind it is a desolate wilderness. Nothing escapes it.
Its appearance is like the appearance of horses, and they run like horsemen.
Like the sound of chariots bouncing over the mountaintops, like the sound of a fiery flame consuming stubble, and like a powerful nation drawn up for battle.
Peoples will tremble before it, and every face will turn black like soot on a cooking pot.
They run like mighty warriors and climb walls like soldiers. Each goes on his own way, and they do not turn aside from their paths.
They do not push one another; instead, each goes along his own path. They fall under the weight of their weapons and do not rise up.
They climb into the cities, run along the walls, climb onto houses, and enter through windows like thieves.
Before him the earth was shaken and the heavens trembled. The sun and moon grew dark, and the light of the stars faded.

The Lord raises his voice before his army, for his camp is exceedingly large, and the one who carries out his command is powerful. For the day of the Lord is great and very terrifying. Who can endure it?
Now, says the Lord, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.
Tear your hearts, not your clothes, and return to the Lord your God, because he is merciful and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in kindness, and he turns away disaster.
Who knows whether he will turn back, have mercy on us, and leave a blessing behind him—fine flour and a drink offering for the Lord your God?
Blow the trumpet in Zion; consecrate a fast; call an assembly.
Gather the people; set apart the congregation. Gather the old people, and gather the young and the nursing infants. Let the bridegroom come out of his room and the bride out of her bridal chamber.

Between the porch and the altar, let the priests, the servants of the Lord, weep and say, “Have pity on your people, Lord! Do not hand over your inheritance to disgrace and to the rule of the nations, so that the nations will not say, ‘Where is their God?’”
Then the Lord became zealous for his land and had pity on his people.
The Lord answered his people and said, “Look, I am sending you grain, wine, and oil so that you will have enough. I will no longer make you an object of disgrace among the nations.

I will drive the northerner far from you and push him into a dry and desolate land, his front toward the eastern sea and his rear toward the western sea. His stench will spread, and his foul smell will rise, because he has acted arrogantly.”
Do not be afraid, land; rejoice and be glad, for the Lord has risen up to act.
Do not be afraid, wild animals, because grass has sprouted in the pastures of the wilderness, the trees have borne their fruit, and the vine and the fig tree have yielded their produce.
People of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, who has given you food in righteousness and sent down rain for you, the early rain and the late rain, as before.
The threshing floors will be filled with grain, and the presses will overflow with wine and oil.
I will repay you for the years that the flying locust, the crawling locust, the cricket, and the stripping locust ate—my great army that I sent against you.
You will eat and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the Lord your God, who has done wonders for you. My people will never again be put to shame.
You will know that I am among Israel, that I myself am the Lord your God, and that there is no other besides me. My people will never again be put to shame.
Afterward I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
Even on male slaves and female slaves I will pour out my Spirit in those days.
I will perform wonders in heaven and on earth: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and dreadful day of the Lord comes.
Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the Lord has said, for the survivors whom the Lord has called.
For in those days and at that time, when I bring back the captives of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them on behalf of my people and Israel, my inheritance, who were scattered among the nations, because they divided up my land.
They cast lots for my people, gave boys as payment for prostitutes, and sold girls for wine, which they drank.

What are you to me, Tyre and Sidon and the whole region of Philistia? Are you repaying me for something? If you inflict injuries on me, I will swiftly and speedily bring your repayment back on your own heads.
Because you took my silver and my gold and brought my beautiful vessels into your temples.
You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to remove them far from their own territory.
Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will bring your repayment back upon your own heads.
I will hand your sons and daughters over to the people of Judah, and they will sell them to Sheba, to a distant nation, for the Lord has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: Consecrate yourselves for war! Rouse the mighty warriors! Let all the fighting men draw near and come up!
Beat your plowshares into swords and your sickles into spears. Let the weak say, “I am a warrior!”
Gather and come, all you surrounding nations! Draw near! There the Lord will shatter your might.
Let the nations rouse themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Ready the sickles, for the harvest is ripe. Come in and tread, for the vats are full and the winepresses overflow, because their wickedness is great.
Multitudes upon multitudes in the valley of decision! For the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.
The sun and moon have grown dark, and the light of the stars has faded.
The Lord will roar from Zion and raise his voice from Jerusalem, and heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will have compassion on his people and strengthen the people of Israel.
You will know that I myself am the Lord your God, who dwells in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will no longer live in it.

On that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all the channels of Judah will flow with water. A spring will flow out from the house of the Lord and water the Valley of Shittim.
Egypt will become a ruin, and Edom a desolate wilderness, because of the violence against the people of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.
Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
I will avenge their blood and will not pardon. The Lord dwells in Zion.
